page_title: WiFi Lens — Wi-Fi Analyzer & Network Diagnostics for macOS

summary.name: WiFi Lens
summary.one_liner: WiFi Lens is a native macOS Wi-Fi analyzer and network diagnostics app that scans 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz networks, with a paid Pro edition and a free open-source edition on GitHub.
use_cases: Finding dead zones in a home or office
Checking whether nearby networks crowd your Wi-Fi channel
Choosing better router channel and band settings
Diagnosing Wi-Fi connection problems on a Mac
Monitoring Wi-Fi over time from the menu bar
Investigating roaming and interface health in small managed networks
summary.what_it_does: WiFi Lens is a macOS app that scans nearby Wi-Fi networks on the 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands and shows signal strength, channel use, and security in readable form. It includes a spectrum scanner, network tables, channel scoring, roaming tests, connection diagnostics, and Network Self-Check, which the page says are in both editions. Pro adds menu bar monitoring, Timeline event history, Statistics, and Insights for ongoing monitoring. The app processes data locally and can expose scan data to compatible AI desktop tools through a local MCP server.
notable: Local-first: no accounts, cloud sync, or telemetry, and data stays on the Mac
Free open-source edition on GitHub alongside the paid Pro edition
Local MCP server lets AI desktops such as Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop read Wi-Fi scan data
Spectrum scanner across 2.4, 5, and 6 GHz bands
caveats: 6 GHz scanning requires Wi-Fi 6E or Wi-Fi 7 hardware; some 6 GHz networks may not show a 6 GHz label due to macOS API behavior
Pro is sold as a one-time purchase through the Mac App Store; Pro adds menu bar monitoring, Timeline, Statistics, and Insights beyond the open-source edition
